title: Upon thorough inspection, all components of the heating and air system were found to be in excellent condition. The thermostat was responsive, and the air filters were clean, ensuring optimal performance. The ductwork showed no signs of leaks or obstructions, and the condenser unit was free of debris. The blower motor operated smoothly, and refrigerant levels were within the ideal range. Overall, the system was functioning efficiently, providing comfort and reliability to the customer.

I performed a follow up service on the 5 ton Carrier rooftop unit, replacing the condenser fan capacitor that was below specifications. I also conducted a thorough deep cleaning of the outdoor coil, which was heavily soiled, to ensure proper heat rejection and condenser airflow. After the service, I operated the unit through both cooling stages, confirming proper 24 volt calls, normal compressor and condenser fan operation, and refrigerant saturation temperatures above freezing. The unit is now cooling effectively. I recommend monitoring performance and setting thermostats no lower than 72–74°F to prevent coil freezing. No further repairs are needed currently.
